messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty P1 triggered — serving-runtime error pattern detected: repeated CUDA illegal memory access on gw-prod-tn-17. Error rate spiking from 0.1% -> 6% in the last 3m. Impact: some text-generation requests returning 500s and OOMs. Notifying on-call.

Sara (oncall): acked. I'm on it — starting triage. Which customers are currently hitting gw-prod-tn-17?

mike (runtime-eng): seeing the same alerts. Logs show CUDA illegal memory access in model-worker container during KV-cache writeback. Likely a kernel race in the custom attention kernel. Sample from container: ```
[2026-03-15T21:04:12Z] E cuda: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS at /workspace/runtime/attn_kernel.cu:214
stack: runtime::dispatch->execute_kernel() -> kv_cache_writeback()
```

jen (sre): metric view: 5 nodes flapping over last 10m, 3 pods OOMKilled, latency p50 spiked from 120ms -> 480ms. Rolling restarts started automatically on the node pool.

Sara (oncall): tagging customers for impact. @liz can you get a quick impact summary for top 5 customers using Dedicated and Hosted? Priority is Hosted public API traffic first.

liz (customer-ops): on it. Preliminary: 4 enterprise customers with Dedicated unaffected (different pool), but Hosted customers using model-xyz are receiving 500s. I have 2 customers already reporting degraded responses. Drafting a status note.

mike (runtime-eng): quick check: nvcc/kernel stack shows possible misaligned memory access when batch sequence lengths > 1024. Repro locally with synthetic load? Trying a targeted repro on staging.

Sara (oncall): mitigation plan options?

alex (ops-lead): options: 1) Drain affected node(s) from service and move traffic to fallback pool (fallback->cpu/quantized variant), 2) Roll back last kernel-level change from yesterday's runtime build, 3) Hotpatch the kernel with bounds checks (slower) and roll forward, 4) Immediate canary rollback of the model-worker image to previous build. We should pick quickest safe move to restore customer traffic.

mike (runtime-eng): rollback of runtime build is fastest. The kernel change landed ~6h ago and touched attention optimizations. I can trigger a controlled rollback to rtime:v3.8.2 which doesn't include the new kernel. That should avoid illegal-address path.

Sara (oncall): do the rollback and coordinate with deploy-bot. I'll start shifting traffic away from gw-prod-tn-17.

deploy-bot: Deployment job queued: rollback-runtime rtime:v3.8.2 -> target pool gw-prod (affected nodes excluded). ETA 2m to start, 8m to complete for one pool.

jen (sre): Prep notes: draining will cause pod reschedules — watch for pod churn and increased latency during migration. I'll open a watch dashboard and set a temporary alert for queue depth > 500.

mike (runtime-eng): pushing rollback now. Command: ```bash
kubectl set image daemonset/model-worker model-worker=redwood/rtime:v3.8.2 -n redwood-prod 
```

mike (runtime-eng): also toggled automatic eviction off on gw-prod-tn-17 to avoid cascading node flaps while we roll.

Sara (oncall): traffic re-route initiated: policy -> fallback-pool (quantized-variants) for new requests to the problem model family. This should reduce error surface while rollback proceeds.

liz (customer-ops): posting interim status to customers: "We're investigating increased 5xxs for text completion; mitigation in progress (rolling rollback and traffic reroute). We'll update in ~15m." Any blockers to sending now?

alex (ops-lead): OK to send. Add note that Dedicated customers unaffected.

(6 min later)

mike (runtime-eng): rollback progress: 3/5 nodes updated, model-workers reporting healthy on new image. Observed fewer CUDA faults on updated nodes. Sample log on node gw-prod-tn-19: ```
[INFO] model-worker v3.8.2 started successfully
[INFO] kv_cache_writeback: succeeded
```

jen (sre): metrics look better: error rate dropped from 6% -> 0.7% across pool; p95 latency recovering. Can't fully clear until all pods replaced.

Sara (oncall): continuing node drains for the two remaining nodes. Keeping @mike in loop for post-mortem.

deploy-bot: Rollback job completed for pool gw-prod. Status: success.

mike (runtime-eng): running a short chaos test: synthetic load with varied sequence lengths — no illegal address errors observed on rolled-back image. Staging repro still shows issue with the new kernel build. Good signal.

liz (customer-ops): updated customer note: "Mitigation completed — rollback successful; some requests may have been impacted for ~18 minutes. Dedicated customers were not affected. We're following up with a post-incident summary and a timeline." Sending.

Sara (oncall): moving to post-incident tasks: 1) PagerDuty incident de-escalation in 30m if stable, 2) Postmortem owner? @mike please own postmortem and root cause analysis, include repro and kernel diff. 3) Customer RC + credit calc.

mike (runtime-eng): taking postmortem. I'll capture kernel diff, run more fuzz tests for sequence boundary conditions, and prepare a remediation plan: revert kernel changes or add bounds-checking + unit tests + CI GPU fuzz.

jen (sre): I'll prepare metrics dashboard and attach traces for affected traces. Also recommend a temporary runbook change: don't auto-evict nodes on OOM spikes until we confirm root cause to avoid cascading.

alex (ops-lead): After postmortem we should plan ML/infra coordination meeting to decide whether to reintroduce the optimization with safety gates.

Sara (oncall): incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Closing timeline in 1h if no regressions. Good job team. :white_check_mark:

(automated) incident-bot: Incident P1 -> mitigated. Details: rollback runtime -> v3.8.2. Actions: postmortem assigned to mike (runtime-eng).
